title: Trimming into Strength
summary: Nvidia valuation motivates a small defensive shift.
coverage_note: All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

claims.reason: A rise in price/sales supports multiple expansion, but the exact contribution requires split-adjusted share prices, revenue and share-count dates. Comparing market-cap growth with sales multiples alone does not quantify the full return decomposition.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.
claims.next_check: Reconcile July 2019 and September 2020 share count, trailing revenue, dilution and split-adjusted prices.

claims.reason: The stated action cut exposure, but subsequent one- and five-year sensitivities reveal substantial foregone gains versus SPY. No reentry rule or expected holding horizon was specified, so this is strong adverse opportunity-cost evidence rather than a fabricated dated forecast failure.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

evidence.title: NVIDIA sale opportunity-cost sensitivities
evidence.finding: Next close September 10, 2020 to September 9, 2021: NVDA adjusted-close +80.32% versus SPY+36.47%; to September 9, 2025: NVDA+1291.12% versus SPY+109.18%. Vendor split/dividend proxy, no costs; one/five-year windows are evaluator-defined.

claims.reason: Replacing equity exposure with short-duration Treasuries generally changes volatility and upside participation. Success depends on the investor's risk objective and subsequent allocation path; no drawdown limit or return benchmark was supplied.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

framework_lessons: Selling requires a reentry rule to audit timing.
assessment: The note is an allocation decision rather than a quantified market forecast. The NVIDIA sale carries a major observed opportunity cost over transparent later windows; that should remain visible without pretending those windows were the author's prediction horizon.
